newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez gains ahead of property deal.
newsitem.headline: Suez gains ahead of property deal.

text.p: Shares in holding group Compagnie de Suez gained on Friday in anticipation of a property asset deal, traders said.
At 1423 GMT, Suez was up 4.90 francs or 2.23 percent at 224.90 while the CAC-40 index was up 1.3 percent.

Financial paper L'Agefi and afternoon daily Le Monde said Suez could sell in the next few days its 4.4 billion franc property portfolio to one of three investment vehicles led respectively by Goldman Sachs, Lehman Brothers and Morgan Stanley.

Suez could make an asset loss of 2.0 to 2.5 billion francs on the deal, rumoured for a long time, but dealers said such a loss had been discounted in the share price while Friday's rise was partly based on relief that the group would finally be unshackled from its property woes.
Suez also benefited from a general sentiment that was boosting the financial sector in the wake of Tuesday's announcement of the UAP /AXA merger plan.
